newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Britain condemns killing of Greek Cypriot.
newsitem.headline: Britain condemns killing of Greek Cypriot.

text.p: A senior British diplomat on Monday condemned the killing by Turkish Cypriot forces of a 58-year-old Greek Cypriot civilian who had crossed into the northern part of the divided island.

Sir David Hannay, Britain's special representative on the Cyprus problem, said after a 90-minute meeting with Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides that "we condemn and we continue to condemn the killing" of any civilian.

The killing of Petros Kakouli on Sunday in the self-proclaimed Turkish Cypriot state raised to four -- three Greek Cypriots and one Turkish Cypriot -- the number of people killed along the buffer zone since August.

"Anything that can be done to make incidents like that less likely to happen would be thoroughly worthwhile," said Hannay, who arrived in Cyprus on Sunday night to continue efforts to end the 22-year-old division of the island.

Cypriot government spokesman Yiannakis Cassoulides called the killing of Kakouli, a retired fireman, "blatant cold-blooded murder". His body was expected to be brought back by U.N. troops later on Monday.
Turkish Cypriot officials said the man had crossed 200 metres (yards) into the self-proclaimed Turkish Cypriot state and ignored warnings to stop.

The shooting happened at 0735 (0435 GMT) near the eastern end of the buffer zone, close to Achna village and territory controlled by British military bases. His body lay on the ground for about four hours before being removed.
Cypriot police said Kakouli, a resident of the nearby village of Avgorou in the government-controlled area of the island, was with his son-in-law collecting snails.
"At one point his son-in-law lost him and then saw him standing with his hands up," a policeman said. "Turkish soldiers shot him once and then walked closer to him and finished him off."
Cypriot Foreign Minister Alecos Michaelides planned to meet ambassadors of the five permanent members of the Security Council on Monday to lodge a protest.

A Turkish Cypriot military spokesman said soldiers had called on Kakouli three times to stop: "He did not. Three warning shots were fired into the area. He attempted to escape. Shots were fired and he was hit."

The official said the Greek Cypriot had "passed through the buffer zone and intruded on (Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus) TRNC territory". Turkey has 30,000 troops in the north of the island, where the Turkish Cypriots live.
Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash told BBC radio the incident was "most unfortunate" but blamed Greek Cypriot intransigence for tension on the island.

Tension on the Mediterranean island has increased since two Greek Cypriots were killed by Turks during protests along the buffer zone in August. The latest shooting occurred near where a Turkish Cypriot soldier was shot dead beside the U.N.-patrolled buffer zone last month.
Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded in 1974 after a Greek-engineered coup on the island. A Turkish Cypriot breakaway state in the north, recognised only by Ankara, was established in 1983.
